title: Hayden Panettiere death: Accidental overdose included fentanyl, coroner’s office says | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

ActressHayden Panettiere, who publicly shared her struggles with early fame and addiction, died from a toxic mix of the opioid fentanyl and other drugs, authorities in South Carolina said Tuesday.

Her death has been ruled an accident, the Greenville County Coroner’s Office said. But thousands of miles away, investigators have been looking into whether the 36-year-old obtained illicit and possibly counterfeit drugsfrom a dealer in Southern California.

Panettiere, who starred in the TV shows “Heroes” and “Nashville,” was pronounced dead at a Greenville apartment on August 16.

Medics responded to a 911 call, found the 36-year-oldin cardiac arrestand were unable to resuscitate her. She was found in the Airbnb apartment, sitting with her legs crossed andher face down, according to a coroner’s report obtained by CNN.

Two men — later identified by police as Panettiere’s boyfriend and his brother — discovered her on a sofa bed. Panettiere was purple, the coroner’s report says. One man administered two doses of Narcan and called 911 after she remained unresponsive.

One of the men said he didn’t know Panettiere had used illegal drugs in recent days, but “she was very good at hiding them,” the coroner’s report said. The coroner found a powdery substance in the actress’s suitcase and pills on a table, which tested positive for fentanyl, the report said.

In the weeks before her death, Panettiere was at a rehabilitation facility in Malibu, California, the coroner’s report says. She spent about two to three weeks there and was recently released.

“Ending a stay at rehabilitation for substance abuse increases the risk of overdose and death through loss of tolerance,” said Dr. Ed Boyer, an emergency medical physician specializing in medical toxicology at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. Boyer was not involved in Panettiere’s case.

Studies have found the risk for overdose death is higher in the period directly after treatment for opioid use disorder – and the month following treatment “is associated with significantly elevated risk,” according to researchers from thePenn State Social Science Research Institute.

The coroner’s office said Panettiere died from the “toxic effects offentanyl,4-ANPP,Alprazolam,Methocarbamol, andQuetiapine.”

On its own, fentanyl can be fatal, said Dr. Kendall Von Crowns, a forensic pathologist who was not involved in Panettiere’s case. But fentanyl combined with 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine “is a deathly mixture that we see often in cases.”

“Alprazolam (Xanax) is commonly abused and methocarbamol (muscle relaxer) in combination without the fentanyl could be fatal at high enough levels,” said Crowns, the chief medical examiner in Tarrant County, Texas.

“All these drugs result in respiratory depression, which means it makes your brain not realize that it’s not getting enough oxygen. You go into a coma and eventually die from anoxic brain damage.”

The presence of 4-ANPP is notable because it’s “a marker for a fentanyl that was not created in a pharmaceutical lab, meaning it’s a clandestine manufactured fentanyl. It can also be seen as a metabolite of fentanyl as well,” Crowns told CNN.

“So this could mean that the fentanyl taken was manufactured illicitly,” he said. But illicitly manufactured fentanyl can contain varying amounts of fentanyl.

“Again, the fentanyl itself could be fatal, but we don’t know the levels based on what we’re looking at.”

Fentanyl and other synthetic opioids are involved in more than half of all overdose deaths in the United States, according to data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

While overdose deaths have dropped significantly over the past few years, the most recent provisional data suggest fentanyl and other synthetic opioids were involved in more than35,000 US deaths in the past year.

Despite concluding the actor’s death was accidental, authorities continue investigating whether anyone might be criminally responsible for providing her with a lethal substance.

Drug Enforcement Administration agents and Los Angeles-area authorities have questioned several people about the circumstances surrounding the California resident’s death, a source familiar with the casesaid last week.

Investigators were looking into whether Panettiere may have takena counterfeit narcoticand whether it may have interacted with any other substances in her body at the time of her death, the source added.

After the actress’s death, an investigator in the Greenville apartment found blue pressed pills and a straw on a table, both of which would later test positive for fentanyl, according to the coroner’s report. A small plastic bag of a white powdery substance was also discovered in a sunglasses case inside her suitcase, the report said.

“The investigation remains ongoing and the circumstances surrounding the case are complex,” Panettiere’s representative, Kasey Kitchen, said in a statement to CNN shortly after the coroner’s report. “We must all continue to remain patient and allow the investigative process to unfold.”

The actress had spoken publicly about herbattles with mental healthand substance abuse.Postpartum depressionandaddictionplagued her young adult years and temporarily halted the career that began when she wasless than a year old.

But this year, Panettiere addressed her struggles in amemoirandspoke publiclyaboutlosing her brother. And her career was making a comeback, with her latest film released in January.

So when the 36-year-old was pronounced dead in the South Carolina apartment building, shock and griefstretched from Hollywood to Ukraine. Panettiere’s ex-partner, former Olympic and world boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, paidtribute to Panettiereand vowed to make suretheir daughter Kayawould always remember her mother.

Panettiere “had been temporarily staying” at the apartment in Greenville, the coroner’s office said in August. The coroner’s office said it was told she planned to spend her birthday in Greenville before flying to Ukraine to visit her daughter.

Her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, and his brother Zach called 911 the afternoon of August 16 to say Panettiere was unresponsive, according to a Greenville police incident report.

The brothers were questioned separately at the scene, and Brian Hickerson gave an officer a bag of Panettiere’s medications, the report said.

The Hickersons have roots in Greenville, where some of their family members live. According to the police report, Brian Hickerson lived in California, and Zach Hickerson lived in Georgia.

Panettiere’s death – along with revelations from her recently released memoir – cast new light on the challenges ofgrowing up in the public spotlight.

Her tragic fate has inspired otherformer child stars to speak outabout the pressure and struggles that often accompany fame at an early age.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Josh Campbell and Elizabeth Wagmeister contributed to this report.

CNN’s Josh Campbell and Elizabeth Wagmeister contributed to this report.
